i0: ***Still*** = something **continues**. ***Yet*** = something we expect **hasn't happened** (in negatives and questions). ***Already*** = something happened **sooner than expected**.
i1: For *just, yet* and *already* with the present perfect, see also [Present Perfect](/blog/grammar/present-perfect/#pp-just-already-yet).
sya-basic.s: ***Still*** = continuing (*It's still raining*). ***Already*** = sooner than expected (*I've already finished*). ***Yet*** = until now, in **negatives and questions** (*Has she called yet? She hasn't called yet.*)
sya-basic.b0.0.3: *She **still** lives with her parents. I'm **still** hungry.*
sya-basic.b1: ***Yet*** usually goes at the **end** of the sentence. ***Still*** and ***already*** usually go in the **middle**.
sya-negatives.t: Still not, not yet, already in questions
sya-negatives.s: ***Still*** in negatives shows **surprise or impatience**: *He **still** hasn't called!* ***Not… yet*** is neutral: *He hasn't called **yet**.* ***Already*** in a question shows **surprise** that something happened early: *Have you finished **already**?*
sya-negatives.b1: In negatives, ***still*** goes **before** the negative auxiliary: *He **still hasn't** paid me.* (not *He hasn't still paid me*)
sya-any-more.t: Not any more, not any longer, no longer
sya-any-more.s: Use ***not… any more / any longer*** (or formal ***no longer***) for something that **stopped**: *I don't live there **any more**. She **no longer** works here.* The opposite is ***still***.
sya-any-more.b1: ***Any more*** and ***any longer*** go at the **end**. ***No longer*** goes in the **middle** (before the main verb, after *be*): *She is **no longer** the manager.*
sya-any-more.b2: Use a **positive** verb with *no longer*: *I **no longer** smoke.* (not *I don't no longer smoke*)
